key_terms.sense: covering the blood of a slaughtered wild animal or bird
key_terms.definition: The Torah commandment to cover with earth the blood of an undomesticated animal or bird after slaughtering it.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Gemara disputes how much of the blood must be covered and which materials may be used to cover it. It also explains why the earth used for this mitzva is not counted among Abraham's rewards.

key_terms.sense: the life-blood that flows at slaughter
key_terms.definition: The main flow of blood that pours out as the animal dies from slaughter. It is distinguished from blood that spurts aside or clings to the knife or the neck.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel reads "its blood" as the blood of the soul, so once it is covered one is exempt from covering the rest. The Rabbis require all the blood and R. Yehuda even part of it.

key_terms.sense: earth as the required covering material
key_terms.definition: Earth or dust. In the laws of covering the blood, it is the material the verse "cover it with earth" requires, which defines what may be used.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Materials qualify either by being a kind of earth in which plants grow or by being called afar in Scripture, such as ashes and gold dust. Beit Shammai accept only actual earth.

key_terms.sense: a generalization that needs its detail for clarity
key_terms.definition: A hermeneutical principle: when a general term cannot be understood without the detail that follows it, the verse is not read by the limiting rule of klal u-frat (generalization and detail).
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rav Mari invokes it to explain why "with earth" does not restrict "and cover it" to earth alone, since the detail is needed to show what kind of covering is meant.

key_terms.sense: corpse impurity conveyed under a roof
key_terms.definition: The impurity a corpse or its parts convey to people and objects under the same roof or overhang, without any contact.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Reddish plasma from a corpse conveys tent impurity only if a revi'it of actual blood is present. The corpse's other liquids are pure.

key_terms.definition: An item impure at the primary level, which renders what it touches impure in the first degree (rishon).
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Tevul Yom Mishnah treats liquids issuing from impure sources as rishon, except liquids that are themselves an av ha-tumah, such as the saliva, urine and semen of a zav.

key_terms.sense: a man impure through a genital discharge
key_terms.definition: A man with an abnormal genital discharge who becomes a primary source of impurity. Certain of his bodily fluids are themselves primary sources of impurity.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Sages decreed impurity on all a zav's liquids because people do not keep away from him. They made no such decree for a corpse, from which people naturally separate.
